messages:
Sophia Park: Team, we need a tight battlecard + 1-slide benchmark callout for the launch and the webinar sign-up page. Two deliverables: 1) Three short claims we can repeat across the blog, slide, and sales cheat sheet. 2) A single-paragraph benchmark blurb (no long tables). Link to my draft: https://redwood.docs/marketing/launch-claims-draft. Please keep field language short and testable.

Jordan Lee: Read the draft. Recommend framing around operational guarantees rather than raw $/token. Suggested claim framing: "Guaranteed tail latency" and "Unit-cost controls". Also propose a tiny flow: outage -> smart routing -> compatible variant -> <200ms added median. That makes the ops story concrete.

Mike Patel: Dropping numbers from the perf harness. Quick chart to back the flow: simulated regional failover preserved 92% throughput and added +185ms median latency when routing to a compatible variant. Note: numbers vary by model size and sequence length; I'll add the callout line: "Tested on 8k seq, median of 10 runs." Avoid per-token price calls unless we specify config.

Anya Gomez: For AB hooks on the landing page I propose two short test lines: 
- "Same API. Clear performance guarantees."
- "Control costs, preserve latency, choose your deployment."
Also prepping two 1-liners for the battlecard rebuttal:
- To Cloud APIs: "We surface SLAs and rollback policies so apps stay live during upstream incidents."
- To infra vendors: "We handle runtime kernel tuning and rollout ops so your infra team doesn't."

Jordan Lee: Good. Add one inbound-lead routing play: tag demo requests by "latency/cost" priority, route high-latency-risk accounts to Dedicated standby in the pitch, and low-risk to Hosted. This helps SDRs pick the right field collateral.

Mike Patel: I created a micro-case paragraph for the PR: "In a simulated cross-region outage we rerouted traffic to a compatible variant; throughput retention: 92%, median latency delta: +185ms, 99th pctl remained within our SLO for 85% of requests. Outcome: graceful degradation, not a full outage." Will add the chart as one image, not a table.

Sophia Park: Great. Two final asks before I lock copy tomorrow: (A) pick the final 3-sentence headline for the blog and webinar hero, (B) one-paragraph benchmark blurb we can paste into the PR. I'll also ask Design for a simple flow visual we can reuse in the battlecard slide. Please vote on the three-line headline options in the doc. :thumbsup: :thumbsdown:

LaunchBot: Reminder: launch-battlecard-review meeting tomorrow 9:30am PT 3. Invite includes #marketing + #sales + PMs.

Jordan Lee: I'll bring the flow visual and the single-slide failover chart. Mike, can you also export an alt text summary for accessibility?

Mike Patel: Yep, exporting PNG + alt text: "Chart: throughput and median latency before/during/after simulated cross-region failover; shows 92% throughput retention and +185ms median latency during failover." Added to doc appendix.

Sophia Park: Perfect. If no objections after the review I'll mark the battlecard as "field-ready" and push to the webinar template. Thanks everyone.
